newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Poor Q1 earnings cast doubt on Philippines growth.
newsitem.headline: Poor Q1 earnings cast doubt on Philippines growth.

text.p: Disappointing first quarter corporate earnings have prompted some analysts to cast doubt on the Philippines' economic growth prospects, but others said there was no direct correlation.

Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities, said the slower income growth, especially of utility firm Manila Electric Co (Meralco) and food and beer firm San Miguel Corp, could signal a general slowdown in the economy.
Meralco, the country's biggest power distributor, only managed sales growth of 5.4 percent in the quarter. There was also a marked reduction in sales to its industrial customers.
San Miguel's operating income slumped by 37 percent in the three months. Sales of the San Miguel flagship beer have been used as barometers of disposable income, particularly in the countryside.
The Philippines is targetting a robust seven to eight percent gross national product (GNP) growth this year, up from 6.8 percent last year.
"A 7.0 to 8.0 percent economic growth? Sounds great. From initial indications, however, it will remain that way: a nice sounding, catchy phrase," Reyes said in a research paper.

Alvin Ang, an economist at All AsiaSecurities, said that aside from the corporate giants, there were fears that cement and construction firms might be affected by the delay in several government infrastructure projects because of a budget impasse which was resolved only in February.
Joy Quintos, the research head of Capitol Securities One, agreed that an earnings slowdown might pull down overall economic production, but did not spell an end to the Philippine boom.
"If we are to put together all these results, then we're not looking anymore at a 7.0 percent growth for this year... There could be some growth, but not that exciting," she said.
The fear was exacerbated by the value of production index, released on Friday, which posted a marginal year-on-year increase of 0.1 percent in February, and a 6.3 percent decline in January.
Volume of production index slipped by 1.8 percent in February, and slid 9.1 percent in January.

"It's too early to say that the Philippine economy is already in trouble. There might be a slowdown in the manufacturing sector, but it is just one of the sectors in the whole economy," an economist at a foreign brokerage house said.
He said the manufacturing sector has been posting lower growth rates since late last year, but the GNP was able to post healthy growth then.
Paul Joseph Garcia, the economist of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, said the first quarter has always been the leanest period.
He added the agriculture, exports and construction might provide the needed push for the GNP to range between 5.5 to six percent in the first quarter of the year.
A government economist said early economic indicators, such as exports growth rates, point to a steady first quarter GNP growth, and maintained that the growth targets for this year still holds.
The government is set to release first quarter GNP and GDP figures by the end of the month.
